title: The Old Grave-Stone

full_text:
In the courtyard of a town house lay an old, worn gravestone that had been moved from a demolished churchyard to pave the well-walk. The children played upon it, jumping over the weathered chisel marks that read: "Here rests Preben Hansen and his beloved wife."

An elderly grandmother sat by the window and looked upon the stone with tears of sweet memory. "I remember Preben Hansen!" she said softly. "He was a prosperous merchant who fed the poor during the great famine, gave dowries to orphan maidens, and brought warmth to every freezing hearth."

The children stopped their play and gathered around her knee, listening with reverence to the record of quiet nobility and charity lived long ago.

The stone had lost its place in the churchyard, and time had worn away its letters; but the fragrant memory of an unselfish life blossomed anew in the hearts of children, proving that goodness is immortal.
moral: Good deeds done in quiet love are never forgotten before the eyes of heaven.
